lesson_title: Profit, Break-even, Interest and Inflation: the Boerewors Stall's Money Story
hook_text: Your stall opens already R290 in the hole. Roll number 73 is the one that saves you — not 72.
clip_script: Sports-day stall, Pietermaritzburg. Batch of 80 boerewors rolls: bread 150, wors 250, onions and sauce 50, gas 30 — R480, so R6,00 each. Sell at R10: that's R4,00 profit a roll — 66,7% on cost. Rich, right? Not yet. The site fee cost R290, paid before the first customer. Every sale pushes R4,00 at that hole — not the full R10, because R6,00 of every sale walks straight back out for ingredients. So: 290 divided by 4 — 72,5. Sell 72 and you are STILL two rand down. Roll 73 tips you into profit. Round up, always. Now the profit goes to the bank: R8 000 at 6%. Year one earns 480. Year two earns 508,80 — more, because the interest started earning interest. Year three: balance R9 528,13. But while your money climbs, so does the trolley: 5% inflation turns next year's R2 400 basket into R2 520. Budget on old prices and you are R120 short before the fire is lit. Two staircases, always racing. Make sure yours climbs faster.
visual_style: A dawn sports field with a glowing R290 pit beside the stall filling coin by coin, roll 73 landing with a triumphant clink; then a split screen of two staircases — a bank balance climbing in green steps and a grocery trolley climbing in red.
mood: Entrepreneurial and urgent, the energy of a sports-day morning where every sale counts.
pacing: Quick through the batch costing, a suspenseful crawl at 72 rolls, a beat of triumph at 73, then the steady climb of the two racing staircases.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and run any stall, sale or savings plan like a business.
